frontier.hypothesis: The idx 89<->90 swap closes if the tail base copy loses its birthing_insn_p LAUNCH_PRIORITY bump, i.e. if the base pseudo stops being single-set WITHOUT costing an instruction.
frontier.mechanism: birthing_insn_p (tools/gcc-2.7.2/sched.c:2570) requires reg_n_sets[dest] == 1; adjust_priority (sched.c:2543) bumps only birthing predecessors to max_priority, and in the backward walk a higher-priority insn is scheduled earlier and therefore EMITTED LATER. Denying the bump makes the base copy tie with the carrier at priority 1 and fall to the schedule_select hazard tie-break.
frontier.next_probe: V11 (routing the else arm's three record stores through p) is dead - it costs an insn and scores 20. Try instead spellings whose extra set of the base is free: (i) set p in the third-if THEN arm only, so the join copy is the second set (the then-arm copy is already propagated away today, so check reg_n_sets in the .greg/.lreg dump BEFORE trusting the source form); (ii) use an EXISTING multi-set local as the tail base instead of the invented p - 'v0' is the obvious one and rejected/tail-base-reuse-v0-hard-conflicts-with-v0.c was measured on the OLD chassis where the block-local scratches still owned $v0, so it must be re-measured on the s9 carrier chassis.

frontier.hypothesis: The idx 29<->32 swap in the first-if else arm is the same birthing/LAUNCH_PRIORITY phenomenon and may fall to the same lever, since s3 is a two-set pseudo (assigned in both arms) and the 'li v0,-1' beside it is single-set.
frontier.mechanism: Same adjust_priority/birthing_insn_p gate (sched.c:2543/2570). In block 2 of the -dS trace the bump lands on insn 67 ('67 (7f000001)' at T-3) and not on the addiu, which is why the addiu is emitted at the head of the block instead of at its tail.
frontier.next_probe: Map the block-2 insn UIDs to source statements from the .combine dump first (do NOT guess the mapping), then test whether making s3 single-set on the else path - or giving the -1 store a second set - flips the pair. Note both residuals are the SAME shape ('addiu rX,s2,3' at the wrong end of its block), so one correct lever may close both and reach 0.
